newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Details of Israeli-PLO deal on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Details of Israeli-PLO deal on Hebron.

text.p: Israel and the PLO sealed on Wednesday a deal to launch Palestinian self-rule in Hebron and on Israeli withdrawals in the West Bank. Here are details of the accord released by Israel's Government Press Office:
-- Israel will withdraw its troops from 80 percent of Hebron within 10 days. Israel will retain security control over 20 percent of Hebron and over Jewish settlers.

-- Hebron will have 400 PLO police armed with 200 pistols and 100 rifles. Four 16-man PLO Rapid Response Teams (RRT) will handle special security cases. Joint approval is needed for rifle-armed RRTs to act in areas adjacent to Jewish enclaves.

-- Joint Israeli-PLO patrols will tour parts of self-ruled Hebron, especially heights overlooking Jewish settler enclaves, and surrounding areas. Joint units to be allowed into Israeli-run areas will handle incidents involving Arabs only.
-- Israel will re-open an Arab market and a main road next to Jewish enclaves, sites closed in 1994 for security reasons.
-- PLO will guard Jewish shrines in areas under its control.
-- PLO has civilian control over Arabs in Israeli-run areas.
RECIPROCAL COMMITMENTS TO INTERIM PEACE DEALS
-- The sides recommitted themselves to a 1995 interim accord signed between the PLO and Israel's previous government.

-- Israel will withdraw from West Bank rural areas in three stages beginning in March 1997. According to a U.S. letter to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu annexed to the accord, the third pullback, to Jewish settlements and "specified military locations", should be completed by mid-1998.
-- The sides will open final-status peace talks within two months after the Hebron redeployment.
-- Israel will release Palestinian prisoners and start talks on issues including the opening of a Gaza airport and a safe passage between the West Bank and Gaza.
-- PLO will complete the revision of articles of its charter calling for Israel's destruction.
-- PLO commits to fight "terrorist" groups, confiscate illegal weapons, keep police force within limits of peace deals, limit governmental activity to self-rule areas.

-- Six of seven "agreed minutes" attached to the accord were at Israel's request not made public, PLO officials said. Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh denied this, however, telling Reuters: "Everything is revealed and there are no secret articles at all." The PLO officials said one article called for immediate talks on the status of al-Ibrahimi mosque in Hebron's Cave of the Patriarchs compound. The Cave is holy to Jews and Moslems as the burial site of the biblical Abraham.
